items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 6:58AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
A series of fronts are expected to move across the Interior on
Sunday and Monday. The initial front on Sunday will bring a band
of snowfall across the area. With this first front, light snow
accumulations are expected.

The next front moving across the Interior on Monday will be
accompanied by warmer temperatures, which could bring the
potential for a light rain/snow mix in the valleys and moderate
snow amounts across higher elevations. This could lead to slick

items.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 24 at 6:45AM AKDT until October 25 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Total snow accumulations of 15 to 30 inches
in the higher terrain, including Red Dog Mine, and 3 to 6 inches
in Noatak. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Noatak Valley and South Slopes of the Western Brooks
Range.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing
snow could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility
items.areas: South Slopes of the Western Brooks Range; Noatak Valley; Upper Kobuk Valleys
items.instruction:
A Winter Storm Warning for snow means severe winter weather
conditions are expected or occurring. This will make travel very
difficult or impossible.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 24 at 6:34AM AKDT until October 26 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:

3 to 6 inches. South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph.

* WHERE...South Slopes of the Central Brooks Range and Atigun Pass.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
will significantly reduce visibility to below one half mile with
areas below one quarter mile at times. Travel will be impacted
especially for high-profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds
